I can't give you test numbers for aug-lr because that run never finished. Its `train.log` shows it crashed with a CUDA out-of-memory error partway through epoch 7 (of 10). It never wrote test predictions or a `metrics.json`. The draft below marks its test results as N/A rather than estimating them:

---

**Topic classifier: results summary**

All three runs used the same 1,000-example test set.

| Run | Config | Test accuracy | Test macro-F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | lr 3e-5, batch 32, no augmentation | 0.806 | 0.805 |
| aug | lr 3e-5, batch 32, augmentation (p=0.3) | **0.829** | **0.828** |
| aug-lr | lr 1e-4, batch 64, augmentation (p=0.3) | N/A | N/A |

- **Aug beats baseline** by about 2.3 points on both test accuracy and macro-F1. It also does better on validation (0.847 vs. 0.821 accuracy).
- **Aug-lr did not finish.** It ran out of GPU memory during epoch 7 of 10, so it has no test results. Its validation accuracy after epoch 6 was 0.839, but that's from an unfinished run and can't be compared with the others.
- **Recommendation:** go with **aug** for now. If we still want to test the higher learning rate, aug-lr needs to be rerun with less GPU memory use, for example batch size 32 or gradient accumulation.

---

The old results table in the README (0.884 / 0.913 accuracy) doesn't match these runs. I left those numbers out of the summary in case your advisor has seen them before.
